Yes, that's the right boundary. Once I've saved something, that entry is mine — the little record I made, with my title and my wording and my labels. If the original page later changes or vanishes off the internet, I absolutely don't want the app quietly deleting my bookmark or rewriting what I'd written to match whatever's there now. That would mean the web changing out from under me could erase my own notes, and then what was the point of saving it. Keep it exactly as it was, and still try the original address when I open it even if the site now throws an error — that's honest about what a bookmark is.

Since you've raised the "page disappears" case, though, let me tell you the thing I'd really wish for there: for a link that dies, having just the title and description isn't always enough — sometimes I saved it because of what was actually *on* that page. So it would mean a lot to me if, when I save something, the app could quietly keep its own copy of the page as it was at that moment, so that even if the original goes dark I can still get back to the content, not just a dead link. I don't need to design that with you right now, but it matters to me and I'd want it in the picture as we go.

That aside, the boundary you described is exactly right.
